The candidate computed λ = (R²/p) / [(1-R²)/df₂] = 2.5055, which is actually the **expected value of the F-test statistic**, not the noncentrality parameter. # Power calculation for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# Fixed linear model with intercept and 3 predictors
# Anticipated multiple correlation: 0.30
# Sample size: 80 participants
# Significance level: 0.05 (one-sided, upper tail)

# Parameters
n <- 80              # sample size (participants)
p <- 3               # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
rho <- 0.30          # multiple correlation coefficient
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Under the alternative hypothesis, R² = rho²
R_squared <- rho^2
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("R-squared (ρ²):", R_squared, "\n")

# Test statistic under null: F ~ F(p, n-p-1)
# Test statistic under alternative: F ~ F(p, n-p-1, λ) noncentral F
# where noncentrality parameter λ = [R² / p] / [(1 - R²) / (n - p - 1)]
# or equivalently: λ = R² × (n - p - 1) / [p × (1 - R²)]

df1 <- p                    # numerator degrees of freedom
df2 <- n - p - 1            # denominator degrees of freedom

cat("\nDegrees of freedom:\n")
cat("  df1 (numerator):", df1, "\n")
cat("  df2 (denominator):", df2, "\n")

# Critical value from central F distribution (null hypothesis)
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)
cat("\nCritical F-value (α = 0.05):", F_crit, "\n")

# Noncentrality parameter under alternative
lambda <- (R_squared / p) / ((1 - R_squared) / df2)
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", lambda, "\n")

# Power: P(F > F_crit | H₁ true) using noncentral F distribution
# pf gives CDF; 1 - pf gives upper tail probability
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("\n=== POWER CALCULATION ===\n")
cat("Power (one-sided upper tail):", power, "\n")
cat("Power as percentage:", round(power * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)
cat("\n")
print(results)

# and residual noise makes up the rest

# Generate X (3 predictors, intercept will be added automatically)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
# Standardize predictors for convenience
X <- scale(X)

# Generate Y with specified multiple correlation
# If R² = rho², then the regression coefficients are structured such that
# Var(X%*%beta) = rho² * Var(Y)
# For simplicity: Y = X%*%beta + noise where
# beta is set such that correlation(X%*%beta, Y) = rho

# Method: Set beta = rho * w where w is the direction
# Then Y = rho * (X%*%w) + sqrt(1-rho²) * noise
# This gives R² = rho² exactly (on average)

w <- rnorm(p)  # direction vector
w <- w / sqrt(sum(w^2))

reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:n_sims) {
  # Generate signal and noise
  signal <- X %*% w
  noise <- rnorm(n)
  
  # Y with structure: true R² = rho²
  Y <- rho * signal + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * noise
  
  # Fit linear model with intercept
  model <- lm(Y ~ X)
  
  # Extract R-squared
  R_sq_obs <- summary(model)$r.squared
  
  # Test statistic: F = [R²/p] / [(1-R²)/(n-p-1)]
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- n - p - 1
  F_stat <- (R_sq_obs / df1) / ((1 - R_sq_obs) / df2)

  F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)

  }

# The candidate computed lambda using: lambda = (R_squared / p) / ((1 - R_squared) / df2)
# But this is missing a factor of n

# Let me check the correct noncentrality parameter formula
# For the global F-test of R² = 0 in linear regression:
# F = [R²/p] / [(1-R²)/(n-p-1)]
# Under H₀: F ~ F(p, n-p-1)
# Under H₁ with true R² = rho²:
#   The noncentrality parameter is λ = rho² * n / (1 - rho²)
#   OR equivalently: λ = [R² / (1-R²)] * (n - p - 1) / p * p = R² * n / (1 - R²)
#   But the pf() function in R expects the noncentrality parameter
#   for the F-distribution test statistic.

# The standard formula for the noncentrality parameter in the context of
# testing R² = 0 is:
# λ = R² * (n - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
# NOT λ = (R²/p) / ((1-R²)/(n-p-1))

# Let me verify both formulas:

n <- 80
p <- 3
rho <- 0.30
alpha <- 0.05
R_squared <- rho^2
df1 <- p
df2 <- n - p - 1

F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)

# Candidate's formula:
lambda_candidate <- (R_squared / p) / ((1 - R_squared) / df2)
power_candidate <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda_candidate)

# Correct formula:
lambda_correct <- R_squared * (n - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)
power_correct <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda_correct)

# Yet another formulation (direct from the F statistic under H₁):
# Under H₁, E[F] = (p + lambda) / (n - p - 1)
# where lambda is defined such that the noncentral F(p, n-p-1, lambda) 
# has this expected value.

cat("=== NONCENTRALITY PARAMETER FORMULAS ===\n\n")
cat("Parameters: n =", n, ", p =", p, ", R² =", R_squared, "\n")
cat("df1 =", df1, ", df2 =", df2, "\n")
cat("Critical F-value:", F_crit, "\n\n")

cat("Candidate's formula: λ = (R²/p) / [(1-R²)/df2]\n")
cat("  λ_candidate =", lambda_candidate, "\n")
cat("  Power =", power_candidate, "\n\n")

cat("Correct formula: λ = R² × df2 / (1 - R²)\n")
cat("  λ_correct =", lambda_correct, "\n")
cat("  Power =", power_correct, "\n\n")

# Let's also verify the relationship:
# The test statistic is: F = [R²/p] / [(1-R²)/df2]
# Under H₁ with true R² = rho², this follows a noncentral F distribution
# with noncentrality parameter λ = (rho² * df2) / [(1 - rho²) * p]
# 
# Actually, let me be more careful. The standard parameterization is:
# If Y ~ N(μ, σ²), and we test H₀: μ = 0 vs H₁: μ ≠ 0,
# the test statistic t = Y / SE ~ noncentral t with noncentrality δ = μ / σ
# 
# For the F-test: F ~ noncentral F(df1, df2, λ)
# where λ is the noncentrality parameter
# 
# For testing R² = 0, the relationship is:
# λ = (true R² / (1 - true R²)) × df2 / df1
# 
# Let's check:
lambda_formula3 <- (R_squared / (1 - R_squared)) * (df2 / df1)

cat("  λ_formula3 =", lambda_formula3, "\n")

# E[F] = (df1 + λ) / (df2 - 2) when df2 > 2
# E[F] should also equal E[(R²/p) / ((1-R²)/df2)]
# Under H₁, E[R²] = rho² (approximately for large n)
# So E[F] ≈ (rho² / p) / ((1 - rho²) / df2) = (rho² × df2) / (p × (1 - rho²))

# Power calculation for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# Fixed linear model with intercept and 3 predictors
# Anticipated multiple correlation: 0.30
# Sample size: 80 participants
# Significance level: 0.05 (one-sided, upper tail)

# Parameters
n <- 80              # sample size (participants)
p <- 3               # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
rho <- 0.30          # multiple correlation coefficient
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Under the alternative hypothesis, R² = rho²
R_squared <- rho^2
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("R-squared (ρ²):", R_squared, "\n")

# Test statistic under null: F ~ F(p, n-p-1)
# Test statistic under alternative: F ~ F(p, n-p-1, λ) noncentral F
# where noncentrality parameter λ = [R² / p] / [(1 - R²) / (n - p - 1)]
# or equivalently: λ = R² × (n - p - 1) / [p × (1 - R²)]

df1 <- p                    # numerator degrees of freedom
df2 <- n - p - 1            # denominator degrees of freedom

cat("\nDegrees of freedom:\n")
cat("  df1 (numerator):", df1, "\n")
cat("  df2 (denominator):", df2, "\n")

# Critical value from central F distribution (null hypothesis)
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)
cat("\nCritical F-value (α = 0.05):", F_crit, "\n")

# Noncentrality parameter under alternative
lambda <- (R_squared / p) / ((1 - R_squared) / df2)
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", lambda, "\n")

# Power: P(F > F_crit | H₁ true) using noncentral F distribution
# pf gives CDF; 1 - pf gives upper tail probability
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("\n=== POWER CALCULATION ===\n")
cat("Power (one-sided upper tail):", power, "\n")
cat("Power as percentage:", round(power * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)
cat("\n")
print(results)

# to cross-check the analytic power calculation

set.seed(42)
n_sims <- 100000
n <- 80
p <- 3
rho <- 0.30
alpha <- 0.05

# Generate data under H₁: true R² = rho²
R_squared_true <- rho^2

# Simulate test replicates
# We'll generate data where the first p predictors explain rho² of variance
# and residual noise makes up the rest

# Generate X (3 predictors, intercept will be added automatically)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
# Standardize predictors for convenience
X <- scale(X)

# Generate Y with specified multiple correlation
# If R² = rho², then the regression coefficients are structured such that
# Var(X%*%beta) = rho² * Var(Y)
# For simplicity: Y = X%*%beta + noise where
# beta is set such that correlation(X%*%beta, Y) = rho

# Method: Set beta = rho * w where w is the direction
# Then Y = rho * (X%*%w) + sqrt(1-rho²) * noise
# This gives R² = rho² exactly (on average)

w <- rnorm(p)  # direction vector
w <- w / sqrt(sum(w^2))

reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:n_sims) {
  # Generate signal and noise
  signal <- X %*% w
  noise <- rnorm(n)
  
  # Y with structure: true R² = rho²
  Y <- rho * signal + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * noise
  
  # Fit linear model with intercept
  model <- lm(Y ~ X)
  
  # Extract R-squared
  R_sq_obs <- summary(model)$r.squared
  
  # Test statistic: F = [R²/p] / [(1-R²)/(n-p-1)]
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- n - p - 1
  F_stat <- (R_sq_obs / df1) / ((1 - R_sq_obs) / df2)
  
  # Critical value at alpha = 0.05
  F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)
  
  # Reject if F > F_crit
  if (F_stat > F_crit) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

# Simulated power
sim_power <- reject_count / n_sims
sim_se <- sqrt(sim_power * (1 - sim_power) / n_sims)

cat("=== MONTE CARLO VERIFICATION (100,000 simulations) ===\n")
cat("Number of simulations:", n_sims, "\n")
cat("Simulated power:", sim_power, "\n")
cat("Simulated power (%):", round(sim_power * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("Standard error:", sim_se, "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(sim_power - 1.96*sim_se, 4), ", ", round(sim_power + 1.96*sim_se, 4), "]\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Power calculation for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# Fixed linear model with intercept and 3 predictors
# Anticipated multiple correlation: 0.30
# Sample size: 80 participants
# Significance level: 0.05 (one-sided, upper tail)

# Parameters
n <- 80              # sample size (participants)
p <- 3               # number of predictors (excluding intercept)
rho <- 0.30          # multiple correlation coefficient
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Under the alternative hypothesis, R² = rho²
R_squared <- rho^2
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("R-squared (ρ²):", R_squared, "\n")

# Test statistic under null: F ~ F(p, n-p-1)
# Test statistic under alternative: F ~ F(p, n-p-1, λ) noncentral F
# where noncentrality parameter λ = [R² / p] / [(1 - R²) / (n - p - 1)]
# or equivalently: λ = R² × (n - p - 1) / [p × (1 - R²)]

df1 <- p                    # numerator degrees of freedom
df2 <- n - p - 1            # denominator degrees of freedom

cat("\nDegrees of freedom:\n")
cat("  df1 (numerator):", df1, "\n")
cat("  df2 (denominator):", df2, "\n")

# Critical value from central F distribution (null hypothesis)
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2)
cat("\nCritical F-value (α = 0.05):", F_crit, "\n")

# Noncentrality parameter under alternative
lambda <- (R_squared / p) / ((1 - R_squared) / df2)
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", lambda, "\n")

# Power: P(F > F_crit | H₁ true) using noncentral F distribution
# pf gives CDF; 1 - pf gives upper tail probability
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("\n=== POWER CALCULATION ===\n")
cat("Power (one-sided upper tail):", power, "\n")
cat("Power as percentage:", round(power * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)
cat("\n")
print(results)
